Tamil Nadu Says CM Vijay’s UK Visit Secures Rs 15,300 Crore Investment Commitments

Chennai, 18 September 2026: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s recent visit to the United Kingdom resulted in investment commitments worth Rs 15,300 crore and the potential to create more than 10,000 direct and indirect jobs, according to the state government. The six-day visit was part of the government’s strategy to attract global investment and support its target of building a USD 1.5 trillion economy by 2036.

The investment commitments span automotive components, engineering, manufacturing, renewable energy, power equipment and Global Capability Centres (GCCs). The government said the latest commitments add to more than Rs 1 lakh crore in investments attracted during the first 100 days of the government.

On 14 September, Samvardhana Motherson International, along with its European and UK-based joint venture partners, committed approximately Rs 11,000 crore towards chassis, engineering, manufacturing, assembly and warehousing facilities in Tamil Nadu. The project is expected to generate around 7,000 jobs.
A European auto component manufacturer also submitted a Letter of Intent identifying Tamil Nadu as its preferred destination for a proposed Rs 3,000 crore investment in India.

In the technology and services sector, Ernst & Young (EY) signed an agreement to establish a GCC under the Build-Operate-Transform-Transfer model along the proposed Mount-Poonamallee GCC corridor in Chennai. The project involves an investment of Rs 1,000 crore and is expected to create around 2,000 jobs.

Swedish Sigma Technology Group is also set to expand its GCC presence in Tiruchirappalli and Chennai through its Indian arm Sreeya Solutions, with around 600 jobs expected in embedded systems and electrification. UK-based Wilson Power Solutions has committed Rs 300 crore towards a facility in Tiruvallur, with around 400 employment opportunities expected.

During the visit, Vijay met Indian High Commissioner to the UK Kumaran Periasamy in London on 12 September to discuss trade opportunities arising from the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement.

The Chief Minister also met executives of the Hinduja Group, including Ashok Leyland MD Dheeraj Hinduja and Finolex Industries MD Prakash P Chhabria. The executives briefed him on progress related to a Rs 2,500 crore MoU signed during the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investors Conclave 2026. The group also expressed interest in expanding investments in renewable energy, particularly wind power, and increasing exports of commercial vehicles manufactured in Tamil Nadu.
The state government said the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investors Conclave had resulted in 97 MoUs worth Rs 67,452 crore, with the potential to create 1,06,998 jobs.

As part of the visit, Vijay inspected the Silverstone Motor Racing Circuit in connection with Tamil Nadu’s proposed Motor Sports City. He reviewed the circuit’s race control, safety and operational facilities and flagged off the 2026 Michelin Le Mans Cup race, in which actor and racing driver Ajith Kumar participated.

The state government also said discussions during the visit covered raw material procurement for Tamil Nadu’s jewellery and textile manufacturers, a proposed UK aerospace and defence delegation to Hosur, a Northern England space delegation’s planned visit to Chennai, and skill development partnerships in financial services.
The government said the visit also explored opportunities to strengthen UK-Tamil Nadu trade and investment ties across multiple sectors.
